subject: Clarify defense-control process + customer notice examples
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acmetech.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acmetech.com, james.clark@acmetech.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Defense control + evidence handling examples for MSA order form

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Our legal team asked for a concrete example of how Redwood would handle a third-party IP claim on customer-generated content — specifically:

- Who receives the infringement notice and when (timing / SLA)
- Whether Acme would get primary defence or be required to cede defence to Redwood for third-party claims related to hosted inference outputs
- What evidence we would supply (logs, prompt text, KV cache snapshots) and turnaround timelines
- How escrow/holdback or insurance interacts with any defense obligations

Can you share an example notice flow, plus any suggested order-form language (narrowed) we could put in the MSA? Attaching the current MSA redline for reference.

Appreciate it — Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Procurement, AcmeTech

Attachments: Acme_MSA_redline_v2.docx (attachment referenced)

Sarah — thanks, forwarding to legal and ops so we can produce a short, actionable example and a proposed order-form paragraph.

Plan:
- Kimberly: can you draft a short defend/control compromise that preserves Acme's notice right but gives Redwood the ability to manage primary defence for third-party claims about outputs? Suggest 1 paragraph + one evidence list.
- Marissa: ops to confirm what evidence we can produce from hosted logs (timestamps, request ids, prompt snippets), and typical turnaround (we usually respond within 5 business days for evidence requests; full investigation can take longer).
- Ben: I'll coordinate with Acme on preferred escalation contacts and confirm if you need a separate holdback or insurance carve-out.

Quick asks for Acme: please confirm whether you need the defence-control clause to trigger on "Redwood-managed models and hosting" only, or also for customer self-hosted/Private deployments. That changes the approach.

I'll follow up with a draft by EOD tomorrow.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Proposed compromise language + evidence list

Ben / team — draft below for discussion before we send to Acme. My aim was to narrow defense-control to typical commercial carve-outs and give Acme notice / participation rights.

Proposed order-form paragraph (short):
"For third-party claims solely alleging that Outputs from Redwood-managed inference services infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, Redwood may, at its option and at Redwood's expense, assume primary control of the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that Redwood: (a) receives prompt written notice of the claim from Customer; (b) provides Customer with reasonably sufficient information to participate in the defense; and (c) does not settle any claim in a manner that imposes obligations on Customer without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. If Redwood elects not to assume defense, Customer shall have the right to defend at Redwood's expense subject to the terms below."

Evidence list to include (short, shareable with customer):
- Request metadata: request id, timestamp, region, model+version
- Prompt snippet: up to 250 characters of the prompt or the specific segment referenced (redact PII)
- Output excerpt: the alleged infringing text (up to relevant excerpt)
- Storage/cache indicators: whether KV cache or prefix was used and related request ids
- System logs: token counts, inference latency traces (ops-only)

Operational notes:
- Ops (Marissa) recommends we commit to producing the metadata and prompt/output excerpts within 5 business days for urgent claims; extended technical evidence (cache dumps, deep logs) may require NDAs and 10–15 business days.
- We should offer a sample evidence template (attached) and a short notice-to-Redwood email address that triggers the workflow.

Potential compromise bullet to offer Acme: limited defense-control scope to "Redwood-managed hosted inference services" and carve out Private deployments. Consider a $X cap on Redwood's indemnity for third-party infringement tied to the order form value — happy to discuss limit mechanics.

If you want, I can prepare track-changes to the MSA paragraph and a one-page evidence playbook for Acme.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proof_of_evidence_template.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acmetech.com>
Cc: legal@acmetech.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Defense control + evidence handling examples for MSA order form

Sarah — thanks for your patience. Attached are: (1) a proposed one-paragraph compromise for the order form; (2) a one-page evidence playbook that lists what Redwood can deliver and the expected timelines; and (3) a small MSA redline that narrows the scope to Redwood-hosted inference only. Summary below.

Key points: 
- Redwood will accept primary defense for third-party IP claims that arise from Outputs from Redwood-managed hosted inference services, subject to the paragraph below.
- Acme will retain notice and participation rights; Redwood will not settle in a way that binds Acme without consent.
- Evidence we can commit to: request id, timestamp, model+version, prompt excerpt (up to 250 chars), output excerpt, basic cache indicators.
- Timeline: metadata & excerpts — 5 business days; deeper operational artifacts — 10–15 business days / may require a mutual NDA.
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) are excluded from Redwood's defense-control obligation in this paragraph.

If that aligns with Acme's risk appetite, Kimberly can produce a clean tracked redline for your legal team to review. Otherwise please let us know the one or two items you can't accept and we will escalate.

Next step: can your legal team confirm whether Acme needs a monetary cap on Redwood's indemnity for these claims or prefers an insurance/holdback approach? If a cap is required, share the preferred structure (flat cap vs. order-value multiple).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

— Ben
